summary.intent: Execute all 13 plans of CipherBox roadmap Phase 70.1 (rotation read-plane durability + deep crash-resume soundness, spanning TS engine, Rust engine twin, and desktop FUSE live-wiring) via wave-based parallel worktree execution, then validate the phase via real desktop-e2e CI across macOS/Linux/Windows, debugging and fixing whatever the acceptance gate surfaces.
summary.outcome: All 13 plans merged and all unit/integration/e2e gates green (sdk-core 363, sdk 362, cargo sdk 152, cargo fuse 108+1, depth-3 e2e 6/6); execution uncovered and fixed three genuine product bugs (dirty-frontier decrypt-before-check ordering in both engines, JsonSidecarFloorStore multi-writer rename race, and a scope-exit rotation revocation bypass + double-publish), plus a desktop mount-lifecycle gap (refresh_sent_shares never wired) and WinFsp coalescing parity; the D-16 real-mount desktop-e2e acceptance passed fully on Linux, passed security invariants on Windows (count-only failure = WinFsp parity gap, now fixed pending CI), and remains blocked on macOS by a newly root-caused FUSE-T publish-queue edge-trigger latency bug (fix in flight, not yet pushed/re-verified).

repo: Worktree-mode subagents must run `pnpm i` themselves since node_modules is gitignored and absent in fresh worktrees.

Rust executors must scope `cargo fmt -p <crate>` instead of `cargo fmt --all`, or workspace-wide formatting drift strands uncommitted changes across unrelated files and blocks `cleanup-wave` with `worktree_dirty`.

Cross-package dist staleness is a real trap: after merging a wave that changes packages/sdk-core, packages/sdk's vitest suite must be re-run only after rebuilding sdk-core's dist, or it silently tests stale code.

The gsd commit helper can report `commit_failed` as a false negative when lint-staged is just slow (or times out at 2 min on large files like ROADMAP.md) — always verify via `git log` rather than retrying.

rust-analyzer/IDE diagnostics (unused import, E0308, E0063, 'never used') repeatedly appeared as stale mid-edit snapshots during concurrent agent edits; only `cargo check`/`cargo test` output is authoritative.

The GSD decision-coverage gate's D-NN bullet parser only accepts 3 forms (`- **D-NN:**`, `- **D-NN — title**`, `- **D-NN: Title.**`); a period-before-closing-`**` form causes it to fail-bail on ALL bullets with '0/N covered', not just the malformed one.

`state.planned-phase` and roadmap-annotate tools can silently no-op (`updated: []` / `updated:false`) when STATE.md/ROADMAP.md don't match their expected anchor format — always verify with git status/diff and hand-edit as fallback.
sdk-e2e vitest has no dotenv loader; `.env` must be `set -a; . ./.env; set +a` sourced into the shell before running, or the harness falls back to a default test-login secret and gets 401.

The WriteQueue journal scanner (`queue.rs`) treats every `*.json` in `cb-journal/` as a JournalEntry and warns+skips anything that fails to parse (including the co-located rotation-high-water floor sidecar) — benign noise, not data loss, since GC only ever deletes `.bin` files by parsed entry id.

CipherBox delete is a soft-delete (move to private recycle bin, keys re-sealed under the bin plane) — structurally equivalent to a move-out-of-scope, which is why deletes (not just moves) trigger scope-exit rotation; same-folder rename does not rotate (gate only fires when parent != newparent).
Desktop-e2e has two separate harnesses: macOS/Linux run `run-all.sh`, Windows runs `run-all.ps1` — a new step added to one does not automatically apply to the other.
`.mts` test helpers in this repo must be invoked via `node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs`, not the `.bin/tsx` shim.

FUSE-T on macOS CI defers `handle_release` by ~40s past when the test stops touching the mount; combined with the fact that the publish queue only drains when a subsequent FUSE op arrives (no wall-clock backstop), a folder's child-add republish can simply never fire on an idle mount — this is latency-only (journal replay is authoritative) but makes CI assertions relying on propagation flaky/failing.
`mkdir` republishes its parent directly in a spawned thread rather than going through the debounced publish queue, making it immune to the edge-trigger stall that affects file writes.

code.finding: collectDirtyFrontier previously called unsealChildReadKey (AEAD decrypt) before checking childPub.generation > childRef.generation for dirtiness; for a genuinely dirty edge whose parent also rotated, decrypting with the parent's current key always throws before the check runs. Fixed by reordering: plaintext generation check first, decrypt only on confirmed-clean edges, dirty edges pushed with nodeReadKey: undefined and repaired via the ECIES checkpoint plane.

JsonSidecarFloorStore::new() built its own fresh Arc<Mutex<()>> per instance even when multiple instances (generation/seq/checkpoint stores in fs.rs) pointed at the identical rotation-high-water.json sidecar and shared a deterministic .tmp rename path — causing ENOENT races. Fixed with a process-global path-keyed lock registry (shared_lock_for) so co-located instances share one lock.

rotate_read_on_scope_exit matched Ok(_) and discarded the RotateReadResult (new read key) while borrowing fs immutably, so the grant-root inode's in-memory read_key was never refreshed after rotation; the subsequent delete-triggered relink republish then resealed the folder under the stale old key and published last, making the newest IPNS record decryptable by the revoked recipient. Fixed by taking &mut CipherBoxFS and writing the new key/generation into the inode.

A covered scope-exit delete triggers both engine.rs's rotate_one+republish_parent (2 new-key publishes when the scope-root has a surviving child) AND a separate old-key relink republish from update_folder_metadata, yielding +2/+3 publishes instead of the expected +1 for the grant-root. Fixed via a new rotate_read_from_node_with_root_children engine API that takes a caller-supplied post-delete children override so the rotation itself is the single authoritative publish, and the redundant relink is suppressed for the shallow covered case.

workflow: When a user challenges an orchestration choice (e.g. 'why is only 1 plan running concurrently'), state the actual reasoning transparently (canary-first caution) rather than assuming intent, then correct immediately by firing the rest of the wave.

Resuming an already-context-loaded subagent (via SendMessage) for a deepened/corrected task is far cheaper than spawning a fresh one that has to re-derive the same root-cause trace — used repeatedly for research extensions and debugger handoffs.

When a debugger/fixer agent's returned diagnostics conflict with its own claimed fix (e.g. 'never used' warnings on code the agent says it wired in), always re-verify authoritatively via a fresh cargo check/test before trusting the summary — repeatedly caught to be stale IDE snapshots, but worth the check given the stakes (security fixes).

For CI-only real-mount acceptance tests, hold multiple independent fixes (e.g. WinFsp parity + macOS timing fix) unpushed until all are ready, to avoid burning a ~30-min real-mount CI cycle per partial fix.

Distinguish 'harness/fixture bug' from 'genuine product bug' explicitly when delegating debugging — a debugger that fixes the wrong side (patching the test to pass) defeats the purpose of an anti-vacuous gate; instruct debuggers not to modify test logic without flagging it as a distinct decision.

friction: Multiple mid-session stale IDE/rust-analyzer diagnostics falsely suggested broken code (unused imports, E0308, E0063, 'never used') during concurrent agent edits, requiring repeated authoritative cargo check/test re-verification to rule out false alarms.
GSD's decision-coverage gate failed opaquely ('0/15 covered') due to a single malformed bullet elsewhere in CONTEXT.md, requiring manual regex archaeology to find the parser's accepted bullet forms.
state.planned-phase and roadmap-annotate tools silently no-op'd instead of erroring, requiring manual verification and hand-editing of STATE.md/ROADMAP.md.
Plan 03's unscoped `cargo fmt --all` left uncommitted formatting drift across 13 unrelated files, blocking cleanup-wave's merge with worktree_dirty.
Wave 3 post-merge gate showed 3 false test failures due to sdk-core dist staleness after a cross-package change, requiring diagnosis before ruling it non-regression.
sdk-e2e authentication failed with a misleading 401 because the harness's vitest config has no dotenv loader and needed the .env manually sourced into the shell.
The depth-3 anti-vacuous e2e fixture (plan 10) was only typechecked, not run live, so its first live run surfaced a genuine product bug that unit tests had been masking via overly permissive mocks.
Desktop-e2e CI round-trips are slow (~15-40 min) and had to be run multiple times (at least 3 full dispatches) as fixes were incrementally discovered and applied.

The D-16 real-mount acceptance surfaced a critical desktop mount-lifecycle gap (refresh_sent_shares never wired) that made every desktop delete/rename EIO, discovered only at the final acceptance leg rather than earlier in unit testing.
Windows and macOS/Linux desktop-e2e run different harness scripts (.ps1 vs .sh), so a new test step added to one silently didn't apply to the other, requiring a second CI round-trip to discover.
open_items: macOS FUSE-T publish-queue idle-mount stall: harness nudge fix + product wall-clock drain backstop fix in flight (debugger a46221ae), not yet committed/pushed/verified.
WinFsp coalescing port for the scope-exit delete path committed (b9b6e5f6b) but not yet pushed or verified by Windows CI.
WinFsp `handle_rename` still has an ungated `dest_ino` removal and replacement-validity-before-gating order gap — narrowed from the original D-15d parity todo, tracked as remaining work.

ROT-04 desktop grant re-mint no-op (`query_grants_rooted_at`/`update_grant`/`delete_grant` as trait default no-ops) — desktop scope-exit rotation currently de-authorizes ALL recipients rather than selectively re-minting for survivors; tracked as a todo, and the D-16 'Bob cut off' assertion currently can't distinguish selective revocation from blanket revocation.

Journal warning skip fix (is_reserved_floor_sidecar) is committed and verified but relies on hardcoded filename matching rather than directory separation — a cleaner (deferred) alternative would relocate the floor sidecar out of cb-journal/ entirely.
Plan 13's Task 2 (human sign-off on the D-16 real-mount acceptance) is still open pending a fully green three-platform CI run.
Phase verification (gsd-verifier, goal-backward) and final phase completion/routing have not yet run — deferred until D-16 is fully green.
